There is no evidence of obfuscation, encoded strings, or any code in the global scope that could download, exfiltrate, or execute malicious payloads during sourcing.

The PKGBUILD for `sonic-frameworks-via` (version 6.31.0) follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. The source is downloaded from the official GitHub repository at `https://github.com/Sonic-DE/sonic-frameworks-via` (a tag-based archive reference), and a valid SHA-256 checksum is provided (`981c6231fc97c2c5466fefee3a76558eea6ae787d18548cd06e88a577ac47771`), so integrity is verifiable. The build process uses the standard CMake workflow: configuration with `-DBUILD_TESTING=OFF`, compilation, and installation into `$pkgdir` via `DESTDIR`. Dependencies (`glibc`, `hidapi`, `libstdc++`, `qt6-base`, `sonic-frameworks-cmake-modules`) are all consistent with a Qt-based desktop keyboard configurator application. There are no suspicious elements: no obfuscated code, no `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or base64-encoded commands, no unexpected file operations, no network requests to unrelated hosts, and no post-install hooks. The entire PKGBUILD is limited to fetching the upstream source, building it, and packaging the resulting binaries. This is the legitimate keyboard configurator application from the Sonic-DE organization, and nothing in the packaging deviates from normal AUR practices or indicates injected malicious code.
